claims.claim: Gregory Thaumaturgus was a Christian bishop of the 3rd century, born around AD 213 to a wealthy pagan family in Neocaesarea (modern Niksar, then the capital of the area of Pontus in Asia Minor).
Gregory Thaumaturgus died around 270, in the reign of Aurelian (270-275).
Gregory Thaumaturgus was consecrated the first bishop of his native city, Neocaesarea, by Phaedimus, the bishop of Amasea.
The Greek, Syriac, and Armenian Catenæ contain fragments attributed more or less correctly to Gregory Thaumaturgus.
Gregory Thaumaturgus's surviving theological writings are in an incomplete state.
